Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Report unnecessary @using directives in Razor files from the command line
Issues.Body:
## Description

Visual Studio shows an unnecessary `@using` directive in a `.razor` file as faded, and it offers a code action to remove the directive. dotnet/razor#8548 added this feature. No command-line tool reports the same problem. A CI pipeline therefore cannot find these directives, and they stay in the code until a developer sees them in the IDE.

`dotnet format` does not find these directives. IDE0005 analyzes C# source only. The Razor source generator makes C# from `.razor` files, and analyzers treat that output as generated code. Thus IDE0005 does not analyze `@using` directives in `.razor` files.

IDE0005 alone also cannot give the correct result for Razor. The generated C# uses fully qualified names for component types. Thus a `@using` that the file needs only to find a component looks unused to the compiler. In dotnet/razor#8548, the Razor tooling solves this problem with a second step. The tooling gets the list of unused directives from Roslyn. Then it removes from that list the namespaces of the components that the file uses. This logic exists only in the IDE tooling.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with `dotnet new blazor`.
2. In `.editorconfig`, set `dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0005.severity = warning`.
3. In `Components/Pages/Home.razor`, add a `@using` directive that `Components/_Imports.razor` already contains. For example, add `@using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Web`.
4. In the same file, add a `@using` directive for a namespace that the file does not use. For example, add `@using System.Text.RegularExpressions`.
5. Run `dotnet build`.
6. Run `dotnet format style --verify-no-changes --diagnostics IDE0005 --severity info`.

## Expected result

The build or `dotnet format` reports the two directives from steps 3 and 4.

## Actual result

The build completes and shows no diagnostic. `dotnet format` exits with code 0 and changes no files. Visual Studio shows both directives as unnecessary.

## Request

Make the logic from dotnet/razor#8548 available outside the IDE. For example, an analyzer that `dotnet build` and `dotnet format` run can supply it. The diagnostic must have these properties:

- It reports a `@using` directive in a `.razor` or `.cshtml` file when the file does not need the directive.
- It reports a `@using` directive that repeats a directive from an `_Imports.razor` file that applies to the file.
- It does not report a directive in `_Imports.razor` only because one component does not use it. dotnet/razor#4521 gives the same exclusion for the IDE.
- It has a severity that `.editorconfig` can set, so that `TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `--verify-no-changes` can fail a CI build.

## Related issues

- dotnet/razor#8548: Visual Studio fades unused `@using` directives in `.razor` files and removes them. This issue asks for the same check outside the IDE.
- dotnet/razor#4521: The IDE code action for IDE0005 in Razor files.
- dotnet/roslyn#72160: `dotnet format` removes `using` directives of Blazor components because of IDE0005. This is the opposite problem.
- dotnet/format#2119: The earlier report of the problem in dotnet/roslyn#72160.
- dotnet/sdk#40427: IDE0005 reports a `using` directive as unnecessary when source-generated code needs it.

Issues.Title: Caching compiler: replay diagnostics
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/86198.

The context for the diagnostics is a separate file instead of being part of the cache key, so that different diagnostic contexts (e.g., across worktrees) can reuse the same cached output if there are no diagnostics (otherwise that's not possible, i.e., compilations with warnings across worktrees will miss the cache, because the diagnostics can contain full paths).

Issues.Title: Support unsafe v2 in declaration generation
Issues.Body:
## What changes

Roslyn's declaration-generation code still uses pointer signatures to decide whether to add `unsafe`. That works for the legacy rules, but not for unsafe v2: a pointer signature can be safe, and an unsafe member can have no pointers in its signature.

This updates symbol-based generation to follow the member's memory-safety rules:

- **V1:** keep the existing behavior, including the distinction between symbol-to-modifier inference and document generation.
- **V2:** emit `unsafe` when `RequiresUnsafeContext` is true. Otherwise, emit `safe` only when the declaration requires an explicit safety choice, such as an extern member or an instance field in a layout-sensitive type. Emit neither when an annotation is optional.

The change adds `DeclarationModifiers.Safe`, `IsSafe`, and `WithIsSafe(bool)`, and wires recognition and emission through C# generation. These public API additions are proposed for review.

Synthetic generation symbols carry the rules version and effective safety information through copying, cloning, and generic construction. Properties and events account for whether the generated declaration has backing storage, since changing accessor bodies can change whether `safe` is required. Getter/setter requirements are handled separately when needed, without marking the whole property unsafe.

## Scope and limitations

This does not change compiler language rules, metadata encoding, or general extern/body generation. It does not try to preserve optional explicit `safe` spelling when inferring modifiers from an existing symbol.

Compiled assemblies expose the effective requires-unsafe contract, but do not distinguish every explicit `safe` annotation from an omitted modifier or reliably preserve the original backing-storage shape. Generation uses the contract and the output shape it knows rather than promising an exact reconstruction of the original source. Whether additional declared-annotation APIs or metadata information would be useful can be discussed separately; they are not added here.

Issues.Title: Record individual analyzer refs from framework/sdk
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-dotnettools/issues/3658

Reloading an .lscache currently restores every C# analyzer from a referenced framework pack, including analyzers MSBuild removed. This can cause duplicate logging generators and enable off-by-default generators in the editor even when command-line builds are clean.

Preserve MSBuild’s actual analyzer selection while keeping caches compact and environment-independent:

- Add frameworkAnalyzerReferences for selected targeting-pack analyzers. 
- Replace sdkAnalyzerPacks with sdkAnalyzerPackageReferences for selected analyzers from SDK-known NuGet packages. 
- Store compressed, pack-relative paths without installation roots or package versions, and load only the recorded files. 
- Keep selections in their target-framework slices so common entries cannot bind to the wrong pack version. 
- Leave metadata-reference pack expansion unchanged. 
- Bump the cache format to version 3 so older readers cannot silently misinterpret the new selection semantics. Version 2 caches require regeneration.

Issues.Title: Fix Razor rename issue with using aliases
Issues.Body:
Found while working on adding proper support for using aliases to Razor, and thought it was worth splitting out to a separate PR.

Sonic gave us two generated C# documents per Razor document, a "decl" and "impl" document, and each one gets all of the using directives emitted to it. Using aliases in C# are document local, however, so when renaming one, Roslyn only (correctly) renamed things in one of the two documents. This meant that there would be compile errors in the result, either from one document still using the old alias, or from the using directive edit being dropped because it was assumed that edits to using directives would be equivalent in both documents.

The solution, and what this PR does, is twofold: 1, detect a rename of an alias, and collect rename edits from both documents, and 2, combine and map edits from both documents to Razor _before_ processing using directives.

Issues.Title: Stop filing Issue Monster Assigner workflow-failure issues
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Set `safe-outputs.report-failure-as-issue: false` for Issue Monster Assigner to stop automated workflow-failure issues such as https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56847.
- Regenerate only its lock file using the existing gh-aw v0.89.21 compiler and runtime pins.

Issues.Title: Do not delay exit waiting for telemetry
Issues.Body:
Resolves https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56815#issuecomment-6483765498

The initial fix was made in INTERNAL on dotnet/dotnet 11.0.100 for GA.

https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-dotnet/pullrequest/67911?_a=files

| Scenario	| Pre-patch | Post-patch
| --- | --- |  ---
| --version, default NativeAOT path	| 2.11 s | 0.21 s
| No-op build, managed CLI + MSBuild logger | 8.76 s | 4.52 s
| Build telemetry overhead versus opt-out | 5.05 s | 0.91 s

The tracerProvider often get blocked on pending HTTP requests from recent Azure Monitor Exporter changes. It is supposed to be a minimal shutdown delay. Pending requests often take 3-5 seconds to complete, which results in extreme exit delay.

The MS Build logger telemetry client calls ForceFlush, which is why the additional change is needed. The defaultTimeout remains as 5 seconds, because it informs network timeout for HTTP requests in options.Retry.NetworkTimeout - since telemetry POST completion time is often around 3-5 seconds, setting this lower would drop telemetry.

--

The DIFFERENCE between this PR and what went into GA:
- Fixed a test only in dotnet/sdk
- I went from 10 to 100 ms because 10ms may not give enough time to write blob storage on slower disks for short lived commands

When merging, prefer these changes.

Issues.Title: Preserve MTP diagnostics and truthful CI reporting
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix native `dotnet test` reporting at the SDK/process boundary:

- Preserve the elected artifact worker's diagnostic enablement, directory, verbosity, file prefix and synchronous-write setting, including response-file and launch-profile arguments. Configuration still flows; test filters, retries, collection and test-timeout arguments do not.
- Keep original reports and the test exit code when optional processing fails, but print a separate `Reporting: degraded` status. An unexpected reporter failure is recorded for the final summary instead of recursively writing through the failing reporter.
- Give `--collect-test-map` bounded parent progress and a collection-specific final status. Finished modules, discovery counts and mapping counts are not reported as passed tests.
- Label interrupted live results as incomplete without adding recovered TRX counts to IPC counts.
- Integrate the visible-silence heartbeat and failure-first compact-summary behavior from [microsoft/testfx#12141](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/pull/12141), source commit `f4d8d35bf45ce0ece75a66e1b197c96684767e48`. Preserve SDK final-exit-code authority, interactive ordering, explicit progress suppression, and the existing handshake classifications.

The original diagnostic-worker failure is visible in public TestFx builds [1655468](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1655468) and [1654893](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1654893). The crash/report-recovery observation came from [1655450](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1655450). Current main already contains the earlier affected-handshake and neutral zero-test fixes; this does not redo those changes.

## Exact composition

| Component | Source/version |
|---|---|
| BEFORE SDK CLI binaries | `c781c3cda4cf87f94291d04223e9146664d4f5f5` |
| Original AFTER SDK capture | `f5838f51c497a70fb60f3ed7e89102ca293b6838` |
| SDK layout | Built `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet`, SDK `12.0.100-dev`, Windows x64 |
| Test applications | Two genuine MSTest applications targeting `net9.0`, running on .NET `9.0.0` |
| Aligned TestFx package source | `f4d8d35bf45ce0ece75a66e1b197c96684767e48` |
| MTP, TRX, CTRF, Azure DevOps and HangDump packages | `2.6.0-preview.26530.102` |
| MSTest SDK/framework/adapter/analyzers | `4.6.0-preview.26530.102` |
| JUnit package / consumer property | `MicrosoftTestingExtensionsJUnitReportVersion=1.0.0-preview.26530.102` |
| Real affected-map/coverage extensions | `18.13.0-preview.26527.4` |

The 32-package candidate feed was built from that exact TestFx source and every package hash was checked against its frozen manifest (`SHA256 6F22349309EBCBA5B1F711059E0A6540AA8F9A675FBB4DBE2FC826D8B9579605`). These candidate versions are **local validation packages**, not published dependencies or an SDK pin update.

The controlled comparison uses the same complete built SDK layout and the same aligned test applications. BEFORE restores the two preserved baseline CLI binaries (`dotnet.dll` and `dotnet-aot.dll`); AFTER uses the final committed build. The native run explicitly prints `AOT test tier: TestModules.`; it is not a managed test of AOT-shaped source.

The captured invocation records retain argv, working directory, source revisions, binary hashes, parent exit codes, stdout/stderr, line timestamps, reports and map snapshots. The excerpts below are selected actual output, not expected-output illustrations.

Path redaction: `<fixture>` and `<evidence>` replace only the machine-local fixture and capture-directory prefixes. All other captured text and exit codes are unchanged.

## BEFORE / AFTER: diagnostic worker

Exact command shape used from the fixture directory (the variables identify each capture's absolute SDK/results/log paths):

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT = 'true'
$env:DOTNET_CLI_CONTEXT_VERBOSE = 'true'
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
$env:TF_BUILD = 'true'
& $sdk test --no-ansi --no-build `
  --test-modules '*\bin\Debug\net9.0\*.UnitTests.exe' `
  --results-directory $results --diagnostic-output-directory $logs -- `
  --report-trx --report-trx-filename '{asm}_{tfm}.trx' `
  --report-ctrf --report-ctrf-filename '{asm}_{tfm}.ctrf.json' `
  --report-azdo --report-azdo-summary `
  --report-junit --report-junit-filename '{asm}_{tfm}.xml' `
  --hangdump --hangdump-timeout 15m --show-test-results failed `
  --diagnostic --diagnostic-verbosity trace `
  --diagnostic-file-prefix reporting-evidence --diagnostic-synchronous-write
```

`TF_BUILD=true` exercises Azure DevOps logging-command emission locally; this does not upload to a real Azure DevOps build. No Azure access token was passed.

BEFORE, parent exit **0**, artifact-worker exit **5**:

```text
AOT test tier: TestModules.
Merging compatible artifacts produced by different test applications...
Invalid configuration for provider 'Platform command line provider' (UID: PlatformCommandLineProvider). Error: '--diagnostic-output-directory' requires '--diagnostic' to be providedArtifact post-processing with '<fixture>\First\bin\Debug\net9.0\First.UnitTests.exe' exited with code 5. Any artifacts that were not merged will be reported individually.
Test run summary: Passed!
  total: 20
  failed: 0
  succeeded: 20
  skipped: 0
```

AFTER, parent exit **0**, successful artifact processing:

```text
AOT test tier: TestModules.
Merging compatible artifacts produced by different test applications...
Test run summary: Passed!
  total: 20
  failed: 0
  succeeded: 20
  skipped: 0
  Out of process file artifacts produced:
    - <evidence>\after-final-worker-apphost\results\merged\merged-3c919add028e7ccc66c14d3bdc6817de.trx
```

Actual files: BEFORE has two original TRX reports and no merged TRX; AFTER retains both originals plus one merged TRX with **20** results, equal to the sum of the originals. CTRF and JUnit also merge. The worker writes a real `reporting-evidence*` diagnostic log containing its `internal-merge-artifacts` invocation. A solution run with intentional test failures keeps parent exit **2** before and after the worker fix.

## BEFORE / AFTER: collection and hidden progress

The real collection command was:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_CLI_ENABLE_AFFECTED_TESTS = '1'
$env:REPORTING_EVIDENCE_SCENARIO = 'slow'
& $sdk test --no-ansi --no-build `
  --project 'First\First.UnitTests.csproj' `
  --results-directory $results --collect-test-map
```

The package actually instruments the test/product assemblies and writes a source-to-test map. This is not a protocol stub. Both runs exit **0** and produce a map containing ten discovered UIDs and product-source mappings.

BEFORE: no parent heartbeat during the 69.39-second run, followed by:

```text
Test run summary: Zero tests ran
  total: 0
  failed: 0
  succeeded: 0
  skipped: 0
```

AFTER: the default 60-second parent heartbeat appeared at **62.732517 seconds from process launch**, followed by:

```text
Collecting test maps: 0/1 module(s) finished. Current module: <fixture>\First\bin\Debug\net9.0\First.UnitTests.dll
Test map collection: Completed.
  modules finished: 1/1
  Module completion is not a test verdict. Discovery and mapping counts do not represent executed test outcomes.
```

A separate real native `--test-modules` run finishes one ten-test module immediately while the second module completes hidden passing tests every seven seconds. BEFORE remains silent and repeats successful module summaries after the artifacts. AFTER emits this actual line at **61.7903221 seconds**:

```text
running... 18 completed, 0 failed, active modules: 1 | last completion: 4s ago
```

Its final verdict/counts precede artifact paths and do not repeat already-printed successful module summaries. The total remains **20**, including the completed module.

## Failure and fallback evidence

An actual `Environment.Exit(57005)` in the net9 test host produces parent exit **7** before and after, with a retained recovered TRX containing nine results. AFTER adds:

```text
Test run summary: Failed!
  total: 9
  failed: 0
  succeeded: 9
Live test results are incomplete for '<fixture>\First\bin\Debug\net9.0\First.UnitTests.dll': 9 result(s) received. Artifact reports may contain additional recovered results; they are not added to these live counts.
Test run completed with non-success exit code: 7. The test host process exited unexpectedly. See: https://aka.ms/testingplatform/exitcodes
```

The handler regression separately supplies a recovered count of **388** with only **1** live IPC result and verifies that the final live total stays **1**, not 388 or 389.

A genuine relaunched fixture worker deliberately returning 5 leaves parent exit **0** for passing tests and **2** for failing tests. AFTER reports the independent degradation while retaining original reports:

```text
Test run summary: Passed!
Reporting: degraded (1 artifact post-processing failure(s)). Original artifacts are preserved; the test verdict is unchanged.
```

## Executed validation

- Full Debug redist and Native AOT product builds: **0 warnings/errors**. Native DLL size is **36,561,920 bytes**, versus **36,480,512** before (**+81,408 bytes**, Debug win-x64).
- Final focused SDK suite: **246 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- Executed regression sensitivity: the initial targeted suite has **5 intended failures on baseline**; the same behavior is green after the fix. Against captured genuine baseline CLI output, **18 of 25 new behavioral assertions fail**; the remaining seven compatibility assertions already pass. Final composed checks: **50 passed, 0 failed**.
- An additional injected reporter-write failure was executed red, then fixed and executed green, preserving the artifact manager's best-effort boundary.
- **17 actual final-head composed cases** cover native DLL/apphost modules, solution/project commands including build, pass/fail, diagnostic worker logs, preserved originals, deliberate worker degradation, opt-out, invalid diagnostics, zero results, crash recovery, actual map collection, native multi-module collection, cancellation and progress suppression.

| Scenario | Parent exit |
|---|---:|
| Passing module/project runs, successful collection, opt-out, reporting-only degradation | 0 |
| Failed tests, including failed tests plus a failed optional worker | 2 |
| Abrupt host exit / recovered reports | 7 |
| Directory without `--diagnostic` | 5 |
| Zero selected results | 8 |
| SDK timeout and cancelled collection | 3 |

Timeout **3** is the existing SDK policy; this PR does not reinterpret it as the unused deadline constant 15.

Repository commands actually executed (the clean native publish preceded the final-head redist build, which republishes the native CLI):

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Layout\redist\redist.csproj --no-restore -c Debug -m:4 -v:quiet /p:Platform=AnyCPU /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true /p:SkipUsingCrossgen=true /p:SkipBuildingInstallers=true /p:SkipBuildingArchives=true -bl:artifacts\log\final-reporting-redist.binlog
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe publish src\Cli\dotnet-aot\dotnet-aot.csproj --no-restore -c Debug -r win-x64 -v:quiet /p:Platform=AnyCPU /p:BuildProjectReferences=false /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true -bl:artifacts\log\reporting-native-publish.binlog
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ArtifactPostProcessingManagerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationLaunchTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalCollectionReportingTests|FullyQualifiedName~SilenceDrivenHeartbeatRendererTests|FullyQualifiedName~MultiProjectRun_WithDiagnostics|FullyQualifiedName~RunAffectedTestsWithoutTestHost_ReportsSelectionAndSummary|FullyQualifiedName~TestCommandParserTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationActionQueueTests"
```

Native commands ran in the same process as the installed Visual Studio C++ environment, with the installed Windows SDK `um\x64`/`ucrt\x64` library paths. Repository tests use the repository-pinned TestFx versions; the separate composed fixture uses the aligned candidate feed above. Localization was regenerated by the build; the vendored manifest and changed Markdown links were checked.

## Explicit integration boundary

This PR does **not** advertise `RequiredPostProcessingSupported` (handshake 19). Ordinary TRX/CTRF/JUnit merging does not prove the newer required Azure DevOps/GitHub summary handoff. Current extensions retain their real per-module CI-summary fallback because main does not yet implement required single-input jobs and an authoritative final-policy `runSummary`.

The complete required-postprocessing contract is addressed in the dependent [#56852](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56852), stacked on this PR; this PR itself does not advertise that capability. This is main-branch Windows x64 evidence, not release-branch/backport sign-off. No downstream SDK pin or feature-gate rollout is included, and nothing is merged.

## Review follow-up: c6405adbf0

The original comparison above remains BEFORE `c781c3cda4cf87f94291d04223e9146664d4f5f5` / AFTER `f5838f51c497a70fb60f3ed7e89102ca293b6838`. The later, user-requested four-comment review batch is revision `c6405adbf0aadab2a0419579f5bffcd72a72764a`, pushed once after combined validation; it does not change those historical captures or claim that they were rerun at the newer revision.

The review batch contains collection callback exception containment, one-failure accounting when warning output fails, discovery JSON precedence, and module-aware progress opt-outs. The shared parent display is disabled if any selected module effectively opts out. All four replies were read back and their threads resolved. The tested working tree was committed unchanged as this revision.

**Targeted proof:** 181 focused SDK cases passed with zero failures/skips. The managed CLI build and Native AOT publish passed. Exact repository commands:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj -c Debug --no-restore -v:quiet -bl:artifacts\log\review-batch-managed.binlog
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ArtifactPostProcessingManagerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalCollectionReportingTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestCommandProgressPolicyTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestCommandParserTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationLaunchTests"
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe publish src\Cli\dotnet-aot\dotnet-aot.csproj --no-restore -c Debug -r win-x64 -v:quiet /p:Platform=AnyCPU /p:BuildProjectReferences=false /p:IlcUseEnvironmentalTools=true -bl:artifacts\log\review-batch-native.binlog
```

The compiled outputs were deployed into the existing complete redist for the following real CLI checks. `<review-fixture>` is a redacted alias for a separate task-local fixture; `$sdk` points to the built redist's `dotnet.exe`. Its `First` project sets `RunWorkingDirectory` to its `run` subdirectory, has a launch profile containing `--progress off`, and has `run\quiet.rsp` containing `--progress off`. `Second` has no opt-out. The package versions are the aligned candidate versions listed above.

From `<review-fixture>`, with `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=false`, `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLE_AFFECTED_TESTS=1`, `MTP_PROGRESS_SILENCE_SECONDS=1`, `MTP_PROGRESS_SLOW_TEST_SECONDS=1`, `REPORTING_EVIDENCE_SCENARIO=slow`, and `REPORTING_EVIDENCE_DELAY_SECONDS=3`:

```powershell
& $sdk test --no-build --no-ansi --project First\First.UnitTests.csproj --no-artifact-post-processing --show-test-results failed
& $sdk test --no-build --no-ansi --project First\First.UnitTests.csproj --no-artifact-post-processing --show-test-results failed --no-launch-profile-arguments
& $sdk test --no-build --no-ansi --project First\First.UnitTests.csproj --no-artifact-post-processing --show-test-results failed --no-launch-profile-arguments -- @quiet.rsp
& $sdk test --no-build --no-ansi --solution Reporting.slnx --no-artifact-post-processing --show-test-results failed
```

| Managed project/solution case | Actual parent heartbeat lines before -> after | Parent exit before -> after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Launch-profile opt-out | 3 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |
| Relative response file in the module working directory | 2 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |
| Mixed modules, one opting out | 2 -> 0 | 0 -> 0 |
| Profile arguments explicitly disabled (control) | 3 -> 3 | 0 -> 0 |

Discovery was also exercised through genuine MSTest/IPC execution in both managed and Native AOT modes:

```powershell
& $sdk test --no-build --no-ansi --project Discovery\Discovery.UnitTests.csproj --collect-test-map --list-tests json
$env:DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT = 'true'
& $sdk test --no-build --no-ansi --test-modules Discovery\bin\Debug\net9.0\Discovery.UnitTests.dll --collect-test-map --list-tests json
```

The discovery contract fixture accepts the collection option through a benign command-line provider while real MSTest discovery runs; it does not collect maps or emulate the wire protocol. This distinction matters because the current AffectedTests extension itself rejects that combination, unchanged by this PR. In both managed/native checks, BEFORE emitted `Test map collection: Completed.` instead of JSON; AFTER the complete stdout parses as schema `1.0`, containing one test container and ten uniquely identified tests, with exit `0` preserved.

These are scoped follow-up results, not a new required-postprocessing integration claim. The contract-gap disclosure above, path redaction, main-only scope, and no pin/backport/merge boundary remain unchanged.

## CI assertion follow-up: 55dc7a3591

The test-only follow-up is `55dc7a35913328057bfcab8446d23e47bb51ffcb`, directly on `c6405adbf0aadab2a0419579f5bffcd72a72764a`. No production code, protocol, package, or frozen composition fixture changed.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Preserve published tool packages when metadata publication fails
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Cherry-pick only e5d5f149daed17a578892cf497627907259c8a47 from #56861, with provenance, onto `release/11.0.1xx`. The original concurrent tool installation changes from #51834 are already present on this branch and are not included again.

When metadata publication fails, preserve the extracted package if either `.sha512` or `.nupkg.metadata` is already visible. Other installs can already accept that package, and NuGet can repair missing metadata under its canonical package lock. The original exception is still rethrown; incomplete extractions without either completion marker are still removed.

Add two fault-injection regression cases around the atomic metadata move. A concurrent install exercises the production shared-cache path; both cases verify retained tool files, unchanged hashes, valid metadata, and subsequent cache reuse without re-extraction.

## Release compatibility

Production changes are identical to the standalone fix in #56861. Adapt tests to this branch's MSTest conventions (`TestMethod`/`DataRow`, `TestAssetsManager`, and `TestContext.CancellationToken`, including the cancellable tool-install lock overload). The separately reviewed `NUGET_PACKAGES` test-isolation issue is intentionally out of scope.

## Validation

- Full SDK build: `build.cmd /bl:3.binlog -verbosity:quiet` succeeded. Existing NuGet Audit warnings in unrelated projects remain; no audit settings were changed.
- Targeted `ToolPackageDownloaderTests` run against the freshly built SDK: **62 passed, 2 Windows-unsupported cases skipped, 0 failed**. Both metadata-publication failure cases passed.
- TRX retained under `artifacts/log/targeted-tests/Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests/20261030-193652-64540/test-results.trx`.

Related: #56861, #51834.

Issues.Body:
Backports #51834 to `release/10.0.4xx`.

Concurrent tool installs, updates, uninstalls, and shared-cache publication can race, causing sharing violations, partial package visibility, or rollback deleting state another operation has already accepted. This backport preserves the original fix's per-version installation locks, package-wide mutation locks, NuGet-compatible atomic publication, archive-identity validation, and contention diagnostics.

## Differences from the .NET 11 implementation

The concurrency fix is essentially the same; the differences adapt it to the .NET 10 branch's existing infrastructure.

| Area | .NET 11 implementation | This backport |
|---|---|---|
| Command execution | Async install/update path, with a caller-provided cancellation token | Retains .NET 10's synchronous command path |
| Lock cancellation | Install/update passes its token into the package-wide mutation lock | Lock helpers still support cancellation, but the synchronous command supplies no token; the five-minute timeout remains |
| Windows owner discovery | CsWin32-generated Restart Manager bindings, conditionally compiled for Windows | Hand-written P/Invoke bindings, matching the release branch's interop approach; guarded by a runtime Windows check |
| Tracing | Activity spans around install, download, extraction, file movement, and runtime-config updates | Retains the release branch's behavior without those newer tracing spans |
| Tests | MSTest attributes and test-context cancellation tokens | xUnit attributes, existing fixtures, and `CancellationToken.None` for test scheduling |

The core guarantees are preserved: identical lock identities and polling/timeouts, package-wide serialization through commit or rollback, NuGet's canonical package lock, archive-identity validation, atomic completion markers, read-only cache reuse, and protection against rollback deleting published shared packages. Linux/macOS owner-discovery code and the new diagnostic messages are unchanged.

Other visible source differences—Newtonsoft.Json instead of System.Text.Json, the older runtime-graph path, and the absence of newer cached-version lookup APIs—were already differences between the branches, not functionality removed from this fix.

## Follow-up correction from review

Commit e5d5f149daed17a578892cf497627907259c8a47 fixes a cleanup issue inherited from #51834: if metadata publication fails after a completion marker is visible, retain the archive and extracted package rather than deleting contents another install can use. The original exception still propagates. The standalone cherry-pick to `release/11.0.1xx` is #56862; its production patch is identical, with tests adapted to that branch's MSTest conventions.

The regression covers failures immediately before and after the atomic metadata move. With metadata present, a concurrent install accepts the package before the writer fails. With only the hash present, NuGet waits on the canonical package lock and repairs missing metadata after the writer fails. Both cases failed before the cleanup fix and pass afterward.

The separate `NUGET_PACKAGES` test-isolation review finding is not addressed by this correction.

## Validation

- Full `build.cmd` succeeded with zero warnings and zero errors for the initial backport.
- File-lock owner tests: 2 passed, 1 Linux-only test skipped on Windows.
- Tool package downloader tests after the cleanup correction: 61 passed, 1 platform-specific test skipped; the changed project and production references built successfully.
- Global tool install, update, and uninstall command tests: 64 passed for the initial backport.
- The package tests were rerun with the inherited `NUGET_PACKAGES` override removed so their per-test `NuGet.config` cache settings took effect; the first run's only failure was the cache override bypassing the test's isolated package directory.

## Risk

Medium, as in the original change: this touches core package publication and global-tool mutation paths. The backport retains the original synchronization and publication behavior, with the cleanup correction above, while avoiding unrelated async, tracing, test-framework, or generated-interop migrations.


## Tactics

### Summary

Concurrent `dotnet tool` installs, updates, uninstalls, and shared-cache publication race with each other, causing sharing violations, partially visible packages, and rollbacks that delete state another operation already accepted. This backport of #51834 adds per-version installation locks, package-wide mutation locks (held through commit or rollback), NuGet-compatible atomic publication, archive-identity validation, and lock-contention diagnostics (including a file-lock owner finder for Windows/Linux/macOS). It adapts the .NET 11 change to the 10.0.4xx synchronous command path, hand-written Windows P/Invoke, and xUnit tests.

### Customer Impact

Users running parallel tool operations (e.g. CI jobs or multiple shells installing/updating/uninstalling the same global tool or sharing a package cache) can hit sharing violations, partially published packages, or tools removed by a competing rollback. The affected scenario is concurrent tool management on release/10.0.4xx SDKs; serial use is unaffected. No workaround is documented in the PR beyond avoiding concurrent operations.

### Regression?

Unknown — not enough information to determine origin. The PR describes a latent race condition rather than a regression from a specific PR or version.

### Testing

- New `FileLockOwnerFinderTests` (2 passed, 1 Linux-only skipped on Windows).
- Expanded `ToolPackageDownloaderTests` (~737 added lines; 59 passed, 1 platform-specific skipped) and install/uninstall command tests (64 passed across global tool install/update/uninstall).
- Full `build.cmd` succeeded with zero warnings/errors.
- Package tests were rerun with the inherited `NUGET_PACKAGES` override removed after one failure caused by that override.
- CI pipeline has been started; results are pending at the time of writing.

### Risk

Medium. About 1,900 lines are added across core package publication and global-tool mutation paths, plus new platform-specific interop (Windows P/Invoke, Linux/macOS owner discovery), but most of that is localization (.xlf) and tests. The core logic mirrors the original .NET 11 fix, and the five-minute lock timeout remains. Risks include lock contention or timeouts in unusual environments and the branch-specific adaptations (synchronous path, no cancellation token passed to the mutation lock).

Issues.Title: dotnetup: simplify or remove the admin mode command gate
Issues.Body:
Follow-up from https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56664#discussion_r4400779318

## Background

Admin mode currently blocks commands by default. Each command declares its admin-mode support through `CommandBase.GetAdminModeSupport` / `AdminModeSupport`, and `AdminModeGate` rejects any command, option, or argument not explicitly allowed. This was kept for the MVP to avoid new commands or options accidentally running in admin mode.

## Concern

The generic allow-list adds complexity that is mostly exercised by the install commands. Commands that don't support admin mode (mainly update and uninstall) could check the mode themselves. Once more commands support admin mode, the gate protects against little that other changes don't already risk.


## Consider

Arguments should likely not be supported by default in admin mode because that increases scope. We might not actually want to do this, because admin mode is made to support C#DK and others. If they don't need the new arguments or options we are adding, all this does is slow down and complicate development for the main-line scenarios which is non-admin mode. If admin mode gets more traction and interest though, perhaps this equation changes.

## Options

1. Remove `AdminModeSupport`, `GetAdminModeSupport`, and `AdminModeGate`. Unsupported commands check the access mode directly, and the install commands reject the options they can't honor (for example `--install-path` and `--muxer` options).
2. Keep a simple per-command allow/deny check, and drop the per-option allow-list.
3. Remove the gate entirely once every command supports admin mode.

Decide as admin mode support expands beyond `sdk install` and `runtime install`.

Issues.Title: dotnetup: select release files by exact filename instead of substring matching
Issues.Body:
Follow-up from https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56664#discussion_r4414630555

## Problem

`ReleaseManifest` selects a release file for a RID with substring and `Contains` checks on file names. A release has many files per RID (archives, installers, symbols, composite packages), so loose matching can pick the wrong artifact, and every new file type that overlaps an existing name makes this riskier.

## Proposal

- Build the exact file name dotnetup expects. `BlobFeedUrlBuilder` already constructs these names.
- Select the release file whose name and RID both match exactly. Treat zero or multiple matches as an error rather than guessing.
- Use the same approach for archives (`.zip` / `.tar.gz`) and Windows installer bundles (`.exe`).
- Add tests for releases that contain similarly named files for the same RID.

Issues.Title: _CreateComHost target up-to-date checks are incorrect
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

There are two bugs here, one masking the other

First, somehow, the `<CreateComHost` file ends up with the same timestamp as the `$(ComHostSourcePath)` it was copied from. I don't really understand how this can happen, since the task uses ResourceUpdater to add the clsidmap, typelibs, etc (and those resources **are** actually present). 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0a4458e8e981fd1b4ddbf3cf0752e3a775f42add/src/installer/managed/Microsoft.NET.HostModel/ComHost/ComHost.cs#L44

Failing to update the output file's mtime breaks the MSbuild inputs/outputs dependency tracking, so the file ends up copying the date of the `$(ComHostSourcePath)` (i.e. the installation date of the .Net SDK) and always looks out-of-date. And if you have parallel builds, you can end up with multiple targets that have share a `<ProjectReference>` all trying to rebuild a file that *should* have skipped as already been up-to-date (via a higher-level project-to-project dependency).

--- 

The second bug (masked by the first, since which makes the outputs *always* out-of-date), is that `Inputs` aren't accounting for the `<CreateComHost TypeLibraries="@(ComHostTypeLibrary)` files. Which would, after the first bug is fixed is fixed, cause it to fail to rebuild the comhost.dll if a typelib changes but the `@(IntermediateAssembly)` assembly didn't.

https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/c781c3cda4cf87f94291d04223e9146664d4f5f5/src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets#L931-L932
needs to be `Inputs="@(IntermediateAssembly);$(ComHostSourcePath);@(ComHostTypeLibrary)"`

### Steps to reproduce

[HelloComHost.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34193635/HelloComHost.zip)

`dotnet build HelloComHost.csproj`

### Expected behavior

After it's been built once, I expect
> Skipping target "_CreateComHost" because all output files are up-to-date with respect to the input files.

### Actual behavior

`dotnet build HelloComHost.csproj` will re-build the HelloComHost.comhost.dll file over.

If you add `-bl`, the binlog shows

```
_CreateComHost
    Building target "_CreateComHost" completely.
    Input file "obj\Debug\net10.0\HelloComHost.dll" is newer than output file "D:\HelloComHost\obj\Debug\net10.0\HelloComHost.comhost.dll".
    Using "CreateComHost" task from assembly "C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\10.0.402\Sdks\Microsoft.NET.Sdk\targets\..\tools\net10.0\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.dll".
    CreateComHost
        Assembly = C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk\10.0.402\Sdks\Microsoft.NET.Sdk\tools\net10.0\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.dll
        Parameters
            ComHostDestinationPath = D:\HelloComHost\obj\Debug\net10.0\HelloComHost.comhost.dll
            ComHostSourcePath = C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\Microsoft.NETCore.App.Host.win-x64\10.0.13\runtimes\win-x64\native\comhost.dll
            ClsidMapPath = obj\Debug\net10.0\HelloComHost.clsidmap
            TypeLibraries
                FooLib.tlb
                    Id = 1
```

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

I can add something like

```xml
  <Target Name="TouchComHost" AfterTargets="_CreateComHost"
          Inputs="@(IntermediateAssembly);$(ComHostSourcePath);@(ComHostTypeLibrary)"
	  Outputs="$(ComHostIntermediatePath)">
    <Message Text="workaround for dotnet/sdk#..."/>
    <Touch Files="$(ComHostIntermediatePath)"/>
  </Target>
```

Issues.Title: macOS single-file self-contained published Mach-O binaries all have same LC_UUID causing local network access problems
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

Using dotnet publish to publish C# apps, when several single-file self-contained Mach-O binaries are published, they all have the same LC_UUID.

This can be confirmed using dwarfdump -u on a Mac.

If the apps require local network access, this causes problems. Something about them all having the same LC_UUID causes newer versions of macOS to behave strangely, and fail to grant local network access to the apps when they try to access the network (a popup should appear allowing the user to grant access, but this doesn't happen).

The problem has been seen on:

Golden Gate 27.1
Sequoia 15.8.1
Tahoe 26.7.1

Problems only arise when more than one .NET app with the same LC_UUID is installed. In the "Settings" -> "Privacy & Security" -> "Local Network" menu on the Mac, the toggles to enable and disable local network access interact in strange ways with the toggle for one app affecting the setting for another.

This can be worked around during the build process by randomising the LC_UUID of the apps before signing them and packaging them, but this feels like a bodge.

Ideally the publish process would re-write the LC_UUID of the published Mach-O binary so that it's unique for each app. 

### Steps to reproduce

Publish several C# apps which require local network access for macOS as single-file self-contained apps.

Install those apps on a Mac, and use dwarfdump -u to confirm they all have the same LC_UUID.



### Expected behavior

I expected different apps' Mach-O binaries to have a different LC_UUID.

### Actual behavior

Different published apps all have the same LC_UUID.

### Is this a regression?

Unknown, as this has been revealed by changes Apple have recently made to macOS, but I suspect not as we've had to patch older software.

### Are there any workarounds?

I can be worked around during the build process by randomising the LC_UUID before signing the apps and building the installer.

Issues.Title: Support required MTP artifact processing and global CI summaries
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Implement the existing TestFx **required artifact post-processing** contract end to end. This is the focused companion stacked on [#56851](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56851), not a duplication of its diagnostic forwarding, collection progress, or vendoring work.

- Honor `RequiredPostProcessorKinds` (handshake field 18), including a **single input**. Optional complete-run processing retains its two-input threshold; truncated runs require the corresponding explicit capability.
- Advertise reply field 19, `RequiredPostProcessingSupported`, only when this invocation can honor both required processing and an authoritative `runSummary`. Help, discovery, collection, explicit opt-out, cancellation, and unsupported worker transports do not receive a false promise.
- Compute one run summary **after** SDK handshake/minimum/zero/ignored-exit policies, using logical live counts, parent wall-clock test duration, and all selected modules—including modules without fragments. Do not sum overlapping retries, module durations, or recovered reports.
- Preserve the handshake's producer-module identity rather than an apphost launch path. Leave an unknown compilation TFM null rather than substituting the running framework. Real composed validation caught the `.exe` versus `.dll` provenance mismatch.
- Exclude unsupported transports **before** worker election so an unsupported candidate cannot steal a required desktop job. Join worker reporting before applying outputs, preserve originals and test policy on reporting failures, accept legal null outputs, and bound a running worker when Ctrl+C arrives.

The contract/ownership decision and compatibility rules are documented in [the contributor guide](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/a629f41ab69bdb8f9c2c6ce63d1edf7b5f1aabfe/documentation/general/dotnet-test-artifact-post-processing.md#required-summary-contract-decision). The source contract was inspected before implementation: [TestFx interface and run-summary invariants](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/f4d8d35bf45ce0ece75a66e1b197c96684767e48/src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform/Extensions/ArtifactPostProcessing/IArtifactPostProcessor.cs), [capabilities](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/f4d8d35bf45ce0ece75a66e1b197c96684767e48/src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform/ServerMode/DotnetTest/IPC/Constants.cs), and [manifest consumer](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/blob/f4d8d35bf45ce0ece75a66e1b197c96684767e48/src/Platform/Microsoft.Testing.Platform/Extensions/ArtifactPostProcessing/ArtifactPostProcessingManifest.cs).

## Stack and exact composition

All **32 package payload hashes** were checked against the frozen aligned manifest: `SHA256 6F22349309EBCBA5B1F711059E0A6540AA8F9A675FBB4DBE2FC826D8B9579605`. Candidate packages are fixture-local; repository tests retain their existing pinned dependencies. No old-extension/new-core-only pairing or repository dependency pin was used.

The final stack deliberately retains the original `6fc4e43c66eb03fb2383ab25a809ff7f4dda81aa` commit as an ancestor so the immutable cross-repository and behavior-removal evidence remains reproducible. The reviewed parent was merged, not rewritten or modified by this layer.

The new regression sources were kept byte-identical across two **buildable behavior-removal comparisons** and restoration; SHA256 receipts and both patches are retained. Removing the worker cancellation token causes the intended ten-second deadline failure after the real child readiness marker; cleanup then terminates that owned child. Compiler/setup errors and zero-test runs are **not** counted as red evidence.

All packages are fixture-local `2.6.0-dev` in isolated caches. Source PR head recorded for the final matched-package replay was `82ec9d46d2e671c02138bc9eedc60d8b1aeeef1d`, containing subsequent documentation/nonshipping-test changes only; shipping source/configuration remained the packed `72a3bc87add2b08c153e8eb56ad2a3631170e33c` snapshot.

Their owned `global.json` pins only the final kit, and `--info` confirms its Base Path/commit, preventing redirection to the earlier6fc SDK. Physical package/cache/Alpha/Beta DLL hashes were checked again. Both actual retained manifests have **32 total /25 passed /1 failed /6 skipped /2 modules**, with parent/manifest exits **2 and0** respectively. Each produces one Azure global publication and one GitHub global artifact, exactly10 global Azure timing rows, retained failed `Beta.Longest` details, the correct separate runner-policy/exit context, and the intentionally populated on-failure step summary. Receipts: `final-sdk-failure-run.json`, `final-sdk-ignored-run.json`, `final-sdk-consumer-provenance.json`, and independently verified manifest/artifact copies. Raw failed-test indicators and details are intentionally not erased by an ignored exit. Azure's strict test indicator and the existing on-failure visibility contract are preserved; the added annotation distinguishes accepted runner policy from raw test outcomes. Diagnostic fixture timings are deterministic input metadata, not a performance benchmark.

Issues.Title: Static web assets: Release build/publish of a net10.0-macos Web SDK project fails - manifest only written per RID, read from the RID-less folder
Issues.Body:
## Symptom

A **`net10.0-macos` Web SDK project** builds in Debug, but `dotnet build -c Release` and `dotnet publish` fail:

```
.../Sdks/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets/targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.References.targets(16,5):
error : Manifest file at 'obj/Release/net10.0-macos/staticwebassets.build.json' not found.
```

## Environment

macOS 27.0 (arm64), .NET SDK 10.0.403, `microsoft.net.sdk.macos` workload 27.0.10742, ASP.NET Core shared framework 10.0.14.

## Minimal repro

`probe.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0-macos</TargetFramework>
    <ApplicationId>com.example.probe</ApplicationId>
    <ServerGarbageCollection>false</ServerGarbageCollection>
    <RunWithOpen>false</RunWithOpen>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
var app = builder.Build();
app.UseStaticFiles();
app.MapGet("/", () => "hi");
app.Run();
```

plus `wwwroot/css/site.css`. No VisioForge or other package involved.

- `dotnet build` (Debug) → succeeds.
- `dotnet build -c Release` → the error above, reported twice.
- `dotnet publish -c Release` → same error.
- `dotnet build -c Release -p:RuntimeIdentifier=osx-arm64` → succeeds.

## Cause

In Release the macOS SDK turns the build into a multi-RID one: `dotnet build -c Release -getProperty:RuntimeIdentifiers` returns `osx-x64;osx-arm64` (`Xamarin.Shared.Sdk.props`, "For release desktop builds we default to universal apps").

The static web assets manifests therefore land per RID:

```
obj/Release/net10.0-macos/osx-arm64/staticwebassets.build.json
obj/Release/net10.0-macos/osx-x64/staticwebassets.build.json
```

while `_CleanupReferencedProjectItemGroups` (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.References.targets:16`) reads `$(StaticWebAssetBuildManifestPath)`, which for that configuration resolves to `obj/Release/net10.0-macos/staticwebassets.build.json` — a path the RID-less build never writes (`obj/Release/net10.0-macos/staticwebassets/` is empty, `dotnet build -c Release -t:GenerateStaticWebAssetsManifest` on the RID-less configuration writes nothing).

In Debug the macOS SDK uses one RID (the host's), the manifest lands in `obj/Debug/net10.0-macos/osx-arm64/`, and the reader finds it.

## Expected

`dotnet build -c Release` and `dotnet publish` succeed for a `net10.0-macos` Web SDK project, either because the RID-less configuration also writes the manifest it reads, or because the reading target is skipped/bound to the RID-specific manifests in a multi-RID build.

## Workaround

Pin a single runtime identifier in the project file:

```xml
<RuntimeIdentifier Condition="$([MSBuild]::IsOsPlatform('MacOS')) and '$(RuntimeIdentifier)' == ''">$(NETCoreSdkRuntimeIdentifier)</RuntimeIdentifier>
```

That yields one build configuration, so the manifest path and the reader agree; `dotnet build -c Release` and `dotnet publish -c Release` then work. Passing `-p:RuntimeIdentifier=osx-arm64` on the command line is *not* equivalent when the project has `ProjectReference`s to multi-targeted (iOS/Mac Catalyst/macOS) projects: the global property flows into those legs and restore fails with `NU1102` for `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.Mono.osx-arm64`.

## Note on the publish path

With the workaround, `dotnet publish -c Release` produces an app bundle whose `Contents/Resources` contains the static web assets only if the project copies them there itself; the macOS SDK's own bundling of `wwwroot` warns `The path '...' would result in a file outside of the app bundle and cannot be used` (`_CollectBundleResources`), which is a separate gap: a `net10.0-macos` ASP.NET Core app has no publishing recipe for its web files.

Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When running unit tests using the "dotnet vstest" command with .NET SDK 11.0.100 RTM, “`vstest.console fails to connect to testhost`" error causing the test execution to fail.

The issue is not reproduced with OOB .NET SDK 11.0.100 RC3 on the same OS environment. The behavior appears to be consistent with the issue reported in [[NETSDKE2E][Regression] Running test project failed with error “failed to connect to testhost...” on NET11.0.100 SDK · Issue #56699 · dotnet/sdk](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56699)

**Application Name:** All UnitTest
**OS:** Windows 11 25H2
**CPU:** X64
**.NET Build Number:** 11.0.100-rtm.26522.141
**App installer checking at：** https://devdiv.visualstudio.com/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/3089610

### Steps to reproduce

1. Download and extract the UnitTest project from [DevDiv bug](https://devdiv.visualstudio.com/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/3089610)
2. Open command prompt and navigate to the UnitTest Project folder.
3. Run "`dotnet vstest MVCBlog.Business.Test.dll`"


### Expected behavior

All tests should run successfully.

```
dotnet vstest MVCBlog.Business.Test.dll
VSTest version 18.11.0 (x64)

Starting test execution, please wait...
A total of 1 test files matched the specified pattern.

Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:    27, Skipped:     0, Total:    27, Duration: 888 ms - MVCBlog.Business.Test.dll (net9.0)
```

### Actual behavior

UnitTest run failed with below error:
```
vstest.console failed to connect to testhost. testhost cannot take part in the connection negotiation that verifies the identity of both processes. This is most likely caused by an outdated Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk package reference in the test project. For more information see: https://aka.ms/vstest/negotiation-error

testhost version: 17.14.1
testhost path: C:\bin\Release\net11.0\publish\testhost.dll

Test Run Aborted.
```

### Is this a regression?

Yes
Verify Scenarios:
1). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148: Pass
2). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-rtm.26522.141: Fail
3). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-6.0.440-servicing.26522.15: Pass
4). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-6.0.441-servicing.26523.5: Fail
5). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-10.0.114-servicing.26520.138: Pass
6). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-10.0.115-servicing.26522.139: Fail
7). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-10.0.403-servicing.26521.108: Pass
8). Windows 11 25H2 + dotnet-10.0.404-servicing.26526.111: Fail


### Are there any workarounds?

_No response_

### dotnet --info output

```console
dotnet --info
.NET SDK:
 Version:           11.0.100
 Commit:            db6a003311
 Workload version:  11.0.100-manifests.08e30c08
 MSBuild version:   18.12.2-1.26522.141+db6a00331

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     Windows

.NET workloads installed:
There are no installed workloads to display.
Configured to use workload sets when installing new manifests.
No workload sets are installed. Run "dotnet workload restore" to install a workload set.

Host:
  Version:      11.0.0
  Architecture: x64
  Commit:       db6a003311

.NET SDKs installed:
  11.0.100 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\sdk]

.NET runtimes installed:
  Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 11.0.0 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
  Microsoft.NETCore.App 11.0.0 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]
  Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 11.0.0 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App]

Other architectures found:
  None
```

### IDE version

_No response_

### Other details

**Findings:**
The issue can also be reproduced with a newly created Unit Test project. A new Unit Test project was created using dotnet-sdk-11.0.100-rtm.26522.141, published with the same SDK version, and then executed using dotnet vstest. The same error was observed:
```
vstest.console failed to connect to testhost. testhost cannot take part in the connection negotiation that verifies the identity of both processes. This is most likely caused by an outdated Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk package reference in the test project. For more information see: https://aka.ms/vstest/negotiation-error

testhost version: 17.14.1
testhost path: C:\bin\Release\net11.0\publish\testhost.dll

Test Run Aborted.
```
